slides.texte_overlay:
7 social hacks that feel like
cheating on a group trip
Offer to handle one thing. The car, the restaurant booking, the playlist. Owning one task makes you useful without becoming the stressed guy trying to organise everything.
Wake up a bit earlier and get the coffee. Everyone loves the friend who appears with breakfast. Small, kind, cheap, and it sets a great mood for the whole group for the rest of the day.
Be flexible about small decisions. "Pizza or sushi? I'm happy with either." Group trips go wrong when everyone fights over details. Easygoing guys make the whole trip better.
Split costs instantly. Keep one shared note of who paid what from day one. Money arguments ruin trips. Clear, fair and fast is the easiest way to keep everyone happy until the very last day.
Before: bored in the car, nothing to say. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a story for every town, castle and old bridge you drive past on the way.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: bored in the car, nothing to say. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Now I've got a story for every town we pass.

slides.texte_overlay: Give people space. Not every hour has to be together. "I'm going for a walk, see you at dinner." A little time alone keeps everyone fresh, relaxed and in a good mood, and the evenings together feel better.
Take the group photo nobody remembers to take. Ask a stranger, get everyone in, send it to the chat that night. That's the one photo everyone keeps and looks back at for years.
